problem_text:
A city planner needs to distribute a fixed budget across 15 different infrastructure projects to maximize the total projected benefit.  
The profile for each project is as follows:  
* Project A: projected benefit 0.187, impact score 0.110, allocation limits [0.028, 0.320]  
* Project B: projected benefit 0.102, impact score 0.267, allocation limits [0.073, 0.619]  
* Project C: projected benefit 0.090, impact score 0.185, allocation limits [0.074, 0.588]  
* Project D: projected benefit 0.045, impact score 0.239, allocation limits [0.025, 0.779]  
* Project E: projected benefit 0.150, impact score 0.195, allocation limits [0.033, 0.793]  
* Project F: projected benefit 0.134, impact score 0.187, allocation limits [0.058, 0.571]  
* Project G: projected benefit 0.196, impact score 0.059, allocation limits [0.089, 0.444]  
* Project H: projected benefit 0.056, impact score 0.291, allocation limits [0.059, 0.635]  
* Project I: projected benefit 0.043, impact score 0.258, allocation limits [0.015, 0.307]  
* Project J: projected benefit 0.145, impact score 0.035, allocation limits [0.057, 0.739]  
* Project K: projected benefit 0.031, impact score 0.259, allocation limits [0.001, 0.870]  
* Project L: projected benefit 0.045, impact score 0.152, allocation limits [0.098, 0.380]  
* Project M: projected benefit 0.173, impact score 0.299, allocation limits [0.004, 0.477]  
* Project N: projected benefit 0.103, impact score 0.182, allocation limits [0.047, 0.689]  
* Project O: projected benefit 0.051, impact score 0.253, allocation limits [0.077, 0.354]  

Each project must receive a budget share that lies within its specified allocation limits, and the sum of all budget shares must equal one. To ensure timely completion, the set of quick-delivery projects Q = {G, L} must together receive at least 0.333 of the total budget.  
Additionally, the overall impact score of the portfolio must not exceed 0.204, and the total projected benefit must be at least 0.069.  
Determine the optimal budget allocation that maximizes the total projected benefit while satisfying all constraints.
